section.heading: ASIC’s power of disqualification—failing to comply with director identification number requirements

content.p: ASIC may disqualify a person from managing corporations for up to 3 years if:
within 7 years immediately before ASIC gives a notice under subparagraph (b)(i), ASIC reasonably believes that the person has contravened subsection 1272D(1); and
ASIC has given the person:
a notice in the prescribed form requiring them to demonstrate why they should not be disqualified; and
an opportunity to be heard on the question; and
ASIC is satisfied that the disqualification is justified, after having had regard to the following:
the person’s conduct in dealing with the Registrar under Part 9.1A (about director identification numbers);
whether the disqualification would be in the public interest;
any other matters that ASIC considers appropriate.
If ASIC disqualifies a person from managing corporations under this section, ASIC must serve a notice on the person advising them of the disqualification. The notice must be in the prescribed form.
The disqualification takes effect from the time when a notice referred to in subsection (2) is served on the person.

section.heading: Transitional—notice of director identification numbers for current directors and alternate directors

content.p: This section applies if, on the day Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the amending Act commences:
a person is a director or alternate director of a company, and was so immediately before that day; and
a director identification number for the person has not been lodged with ASIC (whether in an application to register the company or otherwise).
The company must lodge with ASIC in the prescribed form a notice of the person’s director identification number before the earlier of the following:
the end of the 28-day period applying under subsection 346C(3) for the company for the next response to an extract of particulars by the company;
the end of the 28-day period applying under subsection 205B(4) for the company for the next change in the person’s personal details.

section.heading: Transitional—notice of director identification numbers for current directors

content.p: This section applies if, on the day Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the amending Act commences:
a registered body is a body corporate; and
a person is a director of the body, and was so immediately before that day; and
a director identification number for the person has not been lodged with ASIC (whether in an application to register the body or otherwise).
The body must lodge with ASIC in the prescribed form a notice of the person’s director identification number before the earlier of the following:
the end of the 12-month period starting on that day;
the end of the 1-month period applying under subsection 601CV(1) for the body for the next change in the person’s personal details.

section.heading: Manner and format requirements for lodging with, or giving or providing to, ASIC

content.p: This section applies if a provision of this Act or the Transitional Act requires or permits a person to:
lodge with ASIC a document or information; or
give or otherwise provide to ASIC a document or information.
In order for a document or information to be so lodged, given or provided, the person must meet any manner and format requirements for doing so.
Such manner and format requirements may be:
for a document to be lodged in accordance with paragraph 67(1)(a) or (b)—prescribed or approved in the form mentioned in that paragraph; or
in every case—approved under subsection (4) of this section for documents or information of that kind.
ASIC may in writing:
approve a manner for lodging with, or giving or providing to, ASIC a document or information of a specified kind; or
approve a format for lodging with, or giving or providing to, ASIC a document or information of a specified kind.
ASIC must publish each approval on its website.
Note 1: A manner or format could be electronic.
Note 2: ASIC may approve different manners or formats for different kinds of documents or information (see subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).
Note 3: Specifying a kind of document or information could include referring to the provision of this Act or the Transitional Act that requires it to be lodged with or given to ASIC.

section.heading: ASIC may refuse to receive document or information etc.

content.p: ASIC may refuse to receive document or information etc.
If ASIC considers that a document or information purportedly lodged with, or given or provided to, ASIC under this Act or the Transitional Act:
contains matter contrary to law; or
contains matter that, in a material particular, is false or misleading in the form or context in which it is included; or
is incomplete; or
contravenes this Act or the Transitional Act; or
contains an error, alteration or erasure;
ASIC may refuse to receive the document or information and may make a request under subsection (2).
Note: Paragraph (d) will apply if, for example, any manner and format requirements for lodging, giving or providing the document or information are not met (see subsection 68(2)).
For the purposes of subsection (1), ASIC may request:
that the document or information be appropriately amended or completed, and lodged with or given or provided to ASIC; or
that a fresh document or fresh information be lodged with or given or provided to ASIC in its place; or
if the document or information is incomplete—that a supplementary document, or supplementary information, be lodged with or given or provided to ASIC.
Notice to provide further document or information
ASIC may give a written notice to an entity that purportedly lodges, gives or provides a document or information to ASIC under this Act or the Transitional Act, requiring the entity to:
give to ASIC any other document; or
give to ASIC any information;
that ASIC considers necessary in order to form an opinion as to whether it may refuse to receive the first-mentioned document or information.
Notice must specify day by which entity must comply

The notice must specify the day by which the entity must comply with the notice (which must be a reasonable period after the notice is given). ASIC may specify a later day by giving a written notice to the entity.
Requirement to comply with notice
If the entity does not comply with the notice within the time specified in the notice, ASIC may refuse to receive the document or information first mentioned in subsection (3).
Consequences of refusal to receive
If ASIC refuses to receive a document or information, it is taken never to have been lodged with, or given or provided to, ASIC.

section.heading: Disclosing (including publishing) information on certain registers in the public interest etc.

content.p: ASIC may disclose (including publish) information on a register prescribed for the purposes of subsection 1274A(2) or (3) if ASIC reasonably believes that:
the benefits of making such a disclosure outweigh any risks of doing so; and
after having regard to the following matters, making such a disclosure is in the public interest:
whether making such a disclosure could protect consumers or investors from wrongdoing;
the purpose for which the information was collected;
any harm or adverse impacts for persons (including impacts related to privacy or safety) that could result from making, or not making, such a disclosure;
whether the information is commercially sensitive;
whether making, or not making, such a disclosure could prejudice the proper administration of justice;
any other matters prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this subparagraph;
any other matters that ASIC considers relevant.
Note: ASIC may include with such information any other information ASIC is entitled to access and disclose.
Subsection (1) does not apply to information covered by any of subparagraphs 1274(2)(a)(iab) to (v).
ASIC may make a decision under subsection (1) in relation to particular information or a class of information.

section.heading: Restricting access to information or documents lodged with ASIC, or on ASIC registers, in appropriate cases

content.p: ASIC may, by legislative instrument, impose one or more of the following restrictions:

refuse inspection under subsection 1274(2) by a specified class of persons of a specified class of documents lodged with ASIC;
if, after having regard to the matters in subsection (2) of this section, ASIC reasonably believes that the benefits of the restrictions outweigh the risks of the restrictions.
The matters are as follows:
whether having, or not having, the restrictions could protect consumers or investors from wrongdoing;
the purpose for which the class of information or class of documents was collected;
any harm or adverse impacts for persons (including impacts related to privacy or safety) that could result from having, or not having, the restrictions;
whether the class of information or class of documents is commercially sensitive;
whether having, or not having, the restrictions could prejudice the proper administration of justice;
whether the class of information or class of documents is irrelevant to the purposes of the particular register;
whether the disclosure would be of limited benefit to the public because the class of information or class of documents is outdated or incomplete;
whether the class of information or class of documents is inaccurate, is likely to cause confusion or is likely to mislead the public;
any other matters prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph;
any other matters that ASIC considers relevant.
Subsection 1274(2) applies subject to subsection (1) of this section.
